notes.title: Ghost on the Shore is OUT NOW
notes.notes:
Hello ghosties, 

Three years ago, we began working on a new game. The idea for the core story came to our writer Dagmar Blommaert in a dream in which she had died and could only observe her partner’s immense grief from afar while they mourned, dealt with the loss and eventually moved on. 

We came together as a team to produce a plan for the game. This photo below is a very early series of notes from a brainstorming session we had together, on a rooftop in Ghent, back in 2019. 

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36600567/0d8013768da24a1d2ceb1cc633494627e1c08b25.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36600567/b176929fecc031418cb52f510be44f4fe1b0317f.png[/img][/url]

This wrenching feeling of not being able to let go eventually blossomed into [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1211930/Ghost_on_the_Shore/]Ghost on the Shore[/url], an exploration game about the emotional ties that transcend even death. In the game, protagonist Riley is faced with a headstrong ghost, urging her on an adventure across atmospheric shores, uncovering the islands’ tragic secret. Choices in dialogue shape the bond between the two and ultimately decide Riley's fate.

After seeing such wonderful feedback from players on our first game, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/648390/Maries_Room/]Marie’s Room[/url], a narrative exploration game set within the confines of a single room, we felt the next logical step was to expand on this format with a story set across a series of islands, in the format of a branching narrative with multiple endings. 

After three years, our journey has finally come to a close and we are thrilled that you can now meet Riley and Josh for yourselves as you explore the Rogue Islands and discover what happened to these long-forgotten shores. 

👉 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1211930/Ghost_on_the_Shore/]Play Ghost on the Shore on Steam now[/url] 👈

[previewyoutube=22SNw9AUcOE;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]Exploration and Environmental Storytelling[/b]
While you walk the beautiful landscape of the Rogue Islands, you learn their history through the items left behind. Josh remembers more from his time on the islands, and Riley is encouraged to reveal her dreams, goals and why she is running from her old life.

[b]Immersive Dialogue[/b]
A unique feature that allows the player to make choices in a subtle immersive way. You don't always know how your words will affect the other. Words are powerful tools. Just like in real life, things can become fun, exciting or plain awkward.

[b]Irrevocable Choices[/b]
Every dialogue option is shown only once, which makes your choices definite.

[b]Branching Narrative[/b]
The relationship you choose to build with the ghost defines the narrative branch you get to explore. There are four branches with a different ending for each.

[i]Created by like Charlie, the team behind the award-winning story exploration game Marie's Room.[/i]

[u][b]Features[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Discover the [b]branching narrative[/b] and [b]multiple endings[/b]
[*] Make [b]emotional choices[/b] and [b]experience the consequences[/b]
[*] Immerse yourself into a [b]rich story[/b] and [b]atmospheric setting[/b]
[*] [b]Gather clues[/b] and [b]investigate[/b] what happened
[/list]

[b]RELEASE NOTES[/b]
[list]
[*] The Linux version will come soon. We first need get a third party shader issue fixed.
[*] Will ship with English and German.
[*] We will update about four weeks after the initial release with Spanish, French, Russian, Portuguese and Dutch.
[/list]

[b]Press and Streamer requests[/b]
Press inquiries for Keys please via our press kit page:
[url=https://ashgames.com/press/Ghost_on_the_Shore.html]https://ashgames.com/press/Ghost_on_the_Shore.html[/url]
or by e-mail to press@ashgames.com
Streamers who like narrative games and have a Keymailer account can request a key here:
[url=https://www.keymailer.co/g/games/93009]https://www.keymailer.co/g/games/93009[/url]

notes.title: Ghost on the Shore has a LAUNCH DATE! 📆
notes.notes:
Hi all! George here. 

As you will have gleaned from the title of this post, we officially have a date for the Steam release of Ghost on the Shore: [b]Feb 24th. [/b]

Many of you have been following the development of Ghost on the Shore now for some time and I wanted to take the opportunity to thank you. Your comments throughout development have helped shape and refine the game that we will be releasing here at the end of the month, and [b]we could not have done it without you.[/b]

Whether you have been wishlisting the game since the team first began development, or have recently discovered it via a festival or digital event here on Steam, I wanted to show our appreciation for your support. 

As we do our final pre-flight checks now for takeoff, I wanted to ask one final favour.

If you have a friend or colleague, online or otherwise, whom you think would enjoy a first-person narrative driven adventure such as ours, please do share the game with them. We're a very small team here, and we can truly use all the help we can get. If you believe that games are more than just the tried and true formats we all know and accept, please help spread the word by recommending [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1211930/Ghost_on_the_Shore/]the game on Steam[/url] to a friend, or sharing the news on [url=https://twitter.com/lcharliegames]Twitter[/url], [url=https://discord.com/invite/bTuXP9p]Discord[/url] or another social media platform you use. 

Thanks for all your support, and we will meet you on the shore.

notes.title: Dev Diary #8: Sound Designer Spotlight - Dries Vienne
notes.notes:
[i]What makes an indie game stand out? To us, it’s definitely the quality of all the different elements of a game, coming together. The player will notice the art style and gameplay first. But an immersive writing, relatable voice-over and one-of-a-kind sound design make a truly polished experience.

We are lucky to have two extremely talented sound designers on board - Ward Snauwert and Dries Vienne. Dries originally worked on our first title, Marie’s Room, and then freelanced for Ghost on the Shore. Today we’re happy to announce that he has joined us full-time. Let’s get to know him some more.[/i]

[h1]What was your first instrument?[/h1]

My first instrument was the violin at the age of nine, but I'm not sure anybody would want to be in the same room as me when I play it!

Now I try out almost every instrument I come across. I’m making baby steps on the drums and saxophone at the moment. I used a guitalele for [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d03FEXCIuh0&ab_channel=likeCharlie]Marie’s Room[/url], which’s is basically a tiny guitar with 6 strings. Generally, my main instrument of choice is the piano.

With Ward, we also make all sorts of crazy experimental music for Ghost on the Shore. For example, we’ve recorded the sounds of a diaper for a really nice crackling sound. And we turned a bicycle into an instrument. And this is how we come up with a truly unique soundscape for Ghost on the Shore.

[previewyoutube=TkGgciAXS9Q;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]Any other interesting hobbies?[/h1]

I'm very much a sack of marbles when it comes to hobbies. I tend to find passion in so many things that I end up with way too much. Music, programming, drawing, board games, chess, rollerblading…

I really like the hobbyist culture. Making music in a Youth Center, helps me share knowledge about music and game development. Doing game jams, music jams, art jams and the like. You know - figuring out stuff together.

I also play in the band "[url=https://vi.be/platform/thenealions]Nealions[/url]". We are in the process of planning a release for our first EP.

[previewyoutube=1Gwe3G8f-ww;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]What inspires your music?[/h1]

I often come back to either retro-cyberpunk (greatly inspired by Akira, Blade Runner and Ghost In the Shell), or classical music, especially Chopin. I play hours of Chopin on the piano every day! Those two combined have a surreal romanticized influence.

And of course games! My love for retro shooter 'DOOM' has stuck with me since childhood. I even have a related tattoo. I like it through and through and it inspired me to make games myself.

I also draw inspiration from colorful and whimsical books. I still have tons of pop-up books, and I used to make pop-up scenes myself. They offer a meaningful and comfortable mental space to roam around. We use a similar principle in developing games at like Charlie.

I'm good friends with Kenny & Dagmar, the founders of the studio. The two projects we’ve now worked on together have definitely taught me a lot and influenced my philosophy of creating sound for games specifically. I’m very excited to see the game getting near the finish line. The launch in 2021 will definitely be an emotional one.

[i]If you’d like to personally chat with Dries, please join our [url=http://likecharlie.com/discord]Discord[/url]. We would love to get to know you.[/i]

notes.title: Weekly Update #6: The Heart of Little Rogue, a Lullaby
notes.notes:
The lullaby is a sort of universal leitmotif throughout the game. The songs in the game are all in some way linked to one another. All stemming from this ancient song.

I started out by picking pieces from the title song Flesh and Blood and simplified the melody to fit a lullaby. (You can’t use a rock song to get kids to sleep). I’ve used chords for more melancholy and movement. I made different versions to see which fitted the singer’s voice best.

[previewyoutube=s4t9RNf7m9A;full][/previewyoutube]

The lyrics were inspired by the legend of the Selkie - a  seal-like creature that changes into a woman once she comes on land. She can only return to the sea if she puts her seal skin back on. Now that’s a song! She meets a boy, and because he doesn’t want her to leave he hides her skin. She falls in love, becomes a mother. One day she finds her skin and can’t deny the call of the sea and returns. Every year she comes to the beach to see her children again. She sings this song at a bonfire the night before she goes back to the waves.

[previewyoutube=59eajA-rdeo;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Weekly Update #5: A Family Business
notes.notes:
We’re now a team of eight and rolling like never before. Always ready to tackle a new challenge together! We like to think it’s because we all put a bit of ourselves in the game - from the community manager to the CEO.

The stories don’t end with us. Our friends and families become a part of the team too. They often deliver the handwritings for letters, journals and notes within the scene. And you’ll find many drawings created by the children of our crew members. We love watching our little artists create something that can live on within our game. In a way developing Ghost on the Shore is a family business and combines the stories of us all.

[previewyoutube=dzkRWjziY68;full][/previewyoutube]

Our community is very much part of it too. They have contributed to the game in so many ways! If you’d like to be part of this, we’d love to meet you. Please join our [url=likecharlie.com/discord]Discord[/url] to learn more about our events.

Thank you for reading!
TheKristi

notes.title: Weekly Update #4: Happy Holidays!
notes.notes:
This year has been a busy one for like Charlie. We expanded our team with 3D artist Kaat and are now a team of eight. We had four incredibly talented interns - Marie, Yohan, Jef and Jozef - who helped accelerate development. 

We opened our Discord server and 132 of you joined us on this crazy game development journey. And there are many many more friends following us on our social channels. 

We couldn’t ask for a better community, you’ve helped us with new ideas and brought smiles to our faces every day. We’re lucky to have you and we promise to work hard to get you the game you deserve.

If you’d like to learn more about what goes on behind the scenes, we welcome you to join our [url=likecharlie.com/discord]Discord[/url].

We wish you a Merry Christmas and a wonderful New Year!

notes.title: What inspired a game about emotional ties that transcend death?
notes.notes:
Ghost on the Shore´s core story came to our writer Dagmar in her sleep. In a somber dream, she had died and experienced her partner´s immense grief. Unable to reach out she could only be a witness to her partner eventually dealing with the loss and moving on. The dream left her feeling complicated emotions, that later became a seedling of the story. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36600567/9d309efa4008c5512153521c9161d0cfbde6d878.jpg[/img]


Dagmar was selected for a writing retreat on The Isle of Eigg in Scotland. She spent a week discovering the shores, tales of the locals and the little library in her cabin. Much of the game´s locations and general feel is inspired by what she discovered that week.

There are also many historical themes in the game inspired by true events: young men being drafted into wars, the hardships of living on remote islands, the effects of rich employers arriving in rural areas.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36600567/9d1872e2f697f457b61a5b9c81d78dae2da9af57.jpg[/img]


The Isle of Eigg was too an island that had been bought by a family to turn into a working force, like the Rogue Islands in Ghost on the Shore. Some of the inhabitants even became inspirations for the game. For example, skipper Scruff is a crucial character in the game.

Our motto is to first create characters of flesh and blood, who in a way start having a life of their own. Through them, we get to tell our story, a story that hopefully leaves you feeling like you´ve really been somewhere.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36600567/eb0bf7db2b0ba6172179c1b28188041ddc45b179.jpg[/img]


If this sounds interesting to you, please wishlist [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1211930/Ghost_on_the_Shore/]Ghost on the Shore[/url] and join us in our [url=https://discord.com/invite/bTuXP9p]Discord[/url].

- Kristi & Crew of [i]like Charlie[/i]

notes.title: Inspirations Behind Ghost on the Shore
notes.notes:
Ghost on the Shore is a story and relationship exploration game about ties that transcend even death. You play as Riley, a young woman who finds herself stranded on a desolate island with a headstrong ghost, dead for as long as he can remember.

[h1]The Dream[/h1]
Ghost on the Shore´s core story came to our writer in a dream. In this somber dream, she had died and could experience in great force her partner´s immense grief. Unable to reach out she could only be a witness to her partner eventually dealing with the loss and moving on. The dream left her feeling complicated emotions, that morphed into a seedling of a story.

A little while later Dagmar saw a trailer to the movie [i]Jamie Marks is Dead[/i] and the tagline says "how far would you go to be remembered?". She found it such a strong idea and wanted to do something with it, hence merging it with the dream. A story about love, dying and holding on...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36600567/9c28be8d188c1d72c13594912b375f29b79ae0a5.png[/img]

[h1]The Island[/h1]
Dagmar was selected for a writing retreat on The Isle of Eigg in Scotland. She spent a week there writing throughout, creating the entire outline of the game´s story. She got a lot of inspiration from there while discovering the shores and talking to local people. Much of the game´s locations and general feel is inspired by the misty bogs and bright beaches of the island.

The cabin that Dagmar stayed in had a little library on people and folklore and she binge-read all those. The Isle of Eigg was too an island that had been bought by a family to turn into a working force, like the Rogue Islands in Ghost on the Shore. Some of the inhabitants became inspirations for the game too. There used to be a skipper named Scruff with a famous pet otter on Eigg and we named one of our characters after him.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36600567/cc780a09908bc74ec41d6c22b2f181e3b52be7ac.jpg[/img]

[h1]The People[/h1]
We´re constantly doing a lot of historical research about different islands and their people. In Ghost on the Shore, we tell stories of islanders from the past 200 years. So there are many historical themes infused into it: about young men being drafted into wars, the hardship of living on the islands, how rich families brought small islands to make them a source of profit.

First, we create characters of flesh and blood, who start having a life of their own. Through them, we get to tell our story, a story that leaves you feeling like you´ve been somewhere and known someone.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36600567/f2b63d9e3e792ae9f61e16bbebe30c032ab1d2dc.jpg[/img]

We invite you to wishlist Ghost on the Shore to follow our progress.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1211930/Ghost_on_the_Shore/

[i]- like Charlie team[/i]
